related_questions.question: Can delinquency be removed from a credit report?

text_blocks.snippet: While you can't remove a valid, accurately reported delinquency from your credit report, there are ways to address it. If a late payment is incorrect, you can dispute it with the credit bureaus. For accurate late payments, you can request a "goodwill deletion" from the creditor, especially if you have a strong payment history and a valid reason for the missed payment. Delinquencies typically stay on your credit report for seven years from the date they first became delinquent.

list.title: Disputing Inaccurate Information:
list.snippet: If the late payment is reported incorrectly, you can dispute it with the credit bureaus (Equifax, Experian, and TransUnion).

list.title: Goodwill Deletion:
list.snippet: If the late payment is accurate, you can try requesting a "goodwill deletion" from the creditor. This is a request to remove the negative mark as a gesture of goodwill, particularly if you have a solid payment history and a legitimate reason for the missed payment.

list.title: Impact Decreases Over Time:
list.snippet: Even if a delinquency remains on your report, its negative impact on your credit score will lessen over time, especially as it ages.

list.title: Seven-Year Rule:
list.snippet: Generally, negative information, including delinquencies, stays on your credit report for seven years from the original delinquency date.
